headline: With Treasuries shut for Veterans Day, foreigners buy back 10Y futures and the long end recoups a little of Wednesday's sell-off: the 10Y slips 1.3bp to 3.937% while the 3Y holds at 3.729% on BOK hike pricing, pushing 3s10s to a new 1-year low of 20.8bp
summary: KTBs were mixed in a quiet bull flattener: the 3Y closed unchanged at 3.729% and the 2Y +0.1bp at 3.729%, while the 5Y fell 0.7bp to 3.803%, the 10Y 1.3bp to 3.937% (51st percentile of its 1-year range) and the 50Y 1.5bp to 4.026%; the 30Y held at 4.015%. The front end stayed pinned by a priced November 26 hike, so 3s10s narrowed 1.3bp to 20.8bp, its lowest in a year, and 2s3s is flat at 0.0bp. On the week the 10Y is +8.4bp and month to date −7.1bp. Bills were steady: MSB 91-day 3.192%, CD 3.37% and CP 3.83% unchanged, so CP–CD holds at 46bp (92nd percentile). Spread products widened slightly as KTBs firmed: KDB 3Y 25bp over (81st, +2.5bp on the refit), AAA bank 1Y 41.6bp (91st, +1.3bp), while AA- 3Y was 67.8bp (71st) and KEPCO 3Y 41.7bp (89th).
drivers: US Treasuries: shut for Veterans Day, so the move was all local

The US cash market was closed on Nov 11, so there was no overnight Treasury input: at the 1-year beta of 0.47 the implied KTB 10Y move was zero against an actual −1.3bp, all of it local. The last US close (Nov 10) left the US 10Y at 4.98% and the KTB–UST 10Y gap at −104bp, the widest of the year (0th percentile). Dec Fed hike odds stayed near 91% and the dollar touched a 19-month high, so Thursday night's US 30Y auction and Friday's PPI carry the next global impulse.
Foreigners turn back to buying 10Y futures

After Wednesday's heavy selling, foreigners bought 1,646 3Y and 3,216 10Y futures. The 10Y future rose 14 ticks to 108.70, 2 ticks below our basket fair value of 108.72 (5 ticks cheap on Wednesday), while the 3Y slipped 1 tick to 103.50, still 13 ticks under fair 103.63. The long end recovered while the front end did not, which is why the curve flattened rather than rallied.
KOSPI −0.6% on the Nvidia CEO report and options expiry

KOSPI fell 0.61% to 5,342.73 after reports that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang hit chip names (SK Hynix −1.8%), and institutions sold about KRW 0.7–0.8tn on options expiry; foreigners were small net buyers for a third day. KOSDAQ lost 1.2% to 696.53 and the won firmed 2.9 to 1,330.7. A soft equity day gave KTBs a modest bid but no rotation flow.
Supply: dealer fines meet a lighter calendar

Dealers worry the record KRW 1.6tn FTC fine on 15 primary dealers will make them bid less aggressively; the 50Y auction (Nov 13) and the KRW 2.2tn 10Y auction (Nov 16) are the first tests. Against that, November competitive issuance was already cut by KRW 5tn to 12tn, and foreign bond investment turned to a USD 5.6bn net inflow in October, the first in four months.
data: Solid headline; no change to BOK pricing.
Unanimous hold at 3.00%; a majority open to more tightening
Foreign KRW bond flows, October (KOFIA, Nov 10)
Big long that began to unwind on Nov 11.
Strong; December Fed hike near fully priced.
In line; does not block a November hike.
view: Thursday was a pause, not a reversal: with Treasuries shut the 10Y recouped only 1.3bp of Wednesday's 10bp, all of it local, and the 3Y did not move because a November 26 hike to 3.25% is priced and the 2Y and 3Y sit together at 3.73%.

Over four weeks the 10Y is −24.5bp, of which −7.1bp is Treasuries at the weekly beta of 0.59 and −17.4bp is Korea's own rally; the weekly rotation signal is +1.42 (daily +1.53, down from +1.80), still bond-rally because margin credit is −20% over four weeks and the 10Y trend is down, though the KOSPI part (−0.66) keeps fading.

I expect the 10Y in a 3.85–4.05% range into the BOK meeting; the long from 3.95% is 1.3bp in favour and I keep it, stop 4.10%, target 3.80%, adding at 4.00% if the US 30Y auction or Friday's PPI push Treasuries higher, which would hit KTBs at about 0.4–0.55bp per Treasury bp.
I stay flat 3s10s: at 20.8bp it is a new 1-year low, but the flattening is policy-driven and a steepener needs KOSPI to hold its rebound to Nov 17 first.

The rotation signal has worked better against Treasuries (hedged rally calls right 67% of the time and sell-off calls 69%, against 50% and 57% outright; Sharpe 1.30 vs 0.94, worst drawdown −26bp vs −36bp), so I keep the 10Y long against about 0.5 × US 10Y, with the −104bp KTB–UST gap as the carry cost.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y edged up 0.1bp to 3.729%, 83rd percentile of its 1-year range (average 3.37%), +12.8bp on the week; the 1Y rose 0.6bp to 3.619% (90th). 2s3s is flat at 0.0bp (1st percentile, average 13bp) and 1s2s 11bp (5th). MSB 91-day (3.192%) and CD (3.37%) sit at 1-year highs and price a November 26 hike to 3.25%.
buckets.call: Keep: buy the 2Y above 3.80%, target 3.65%, stop 3.90%. Not triggered (7bp away).

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s flattened 1.3bp to 20.8bp, a new 1-year low (0th percentile, average 40bp), as foreigners bought 10Y futures and the hike-priced front end held. The 3s5s10s fly is −6.0bp (3rd percentile, average 4.3bp), so the 5Y stays rich to the wings. Our steepener from 29bp was stopped on Nov 5.
buckets.call: Stay flat. KOSPI slipped 0.6% but holds above 5,300; re-enter the steepener (3 × 3Y vs 1 × 10Y futures, DV01 about KRW 86k each side) only if it holds to Nov 17, target 30bp, stop 17bp.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 3.937% is at the 51st percentile of a 3.25–4.60% range (average 3.91%). The long opened at 3.95% on Wednesday is 1.3bp in favour. Thursday's −1.3bp had no Treasury input (US closed) and came with foreign futures buying; the 10Y future closed 2 ticks below fair value, from 5 ticks.
buckets.call: Long from 3.95%, add at 4.00%, stop 4.10%, target 3.80%; prefer it against about 0.5 × US 10Y. Open, +1.3bp.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s narrowed 1.5bp to +1.1bp, 90th percentile (average −9.3bp), as the 50Y fell 1.5bp and the 30Y held, so the switch from +2.5bp is now 1.4bp in favour. 20s30s is −3.0bp and the 10s20s30s fly 13.8bp (78th), so the 20Y stays cheap. On Wednesday's trades 24-2 2054 was 13.6bp and 25-7 2055 12bp rich to the curve; the 50Y auction on Nov 13 is the near-term risk.
buckets.call: Keep the 30Y into 50Y switch from +2.5bp; target −3bp, stop +6bp. Open, 1.4bp in favour.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: The KDB fit (20 trades) puts the 3Y 25.2bp over KTB, 81st percentile (average 19bp), up 2.5bp as KTBs firmed, so the overweight from about 26bp is 0.8bp in favour. The 1Y fit is 30bp over (73rd) and KOFIA's 1Y KDB quote 27.3bp (67th, average 23.6bp). KEXIM has only 3 trades (low confidence), so ignore its 38bp reading.
buckets.call: Hold from ~26bp; target 20bp, stop 28bp (2.8bp away). Open.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (33-trade fit) is 41.6bp over the 1Y KTB, 91st percentile (average 31bp), 1.3bp wider; the 3Y is 34bp over (80th). CD 3.37% and CP 3.83% were unchanged, so CP–CD stays 46bp (92nd, average 28bp) and CD–MSB91 17.8bp (31st). IBK 1Y (26 trades) is 32.5bp over, 77th percentile.
buckets.call: No change: prefer KDB over bank debentures; revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y slipped 0.3bp to 4.407% with the KTB 3Y unchanged, so the spread is 67.8bp (71st percentile, average 61bp). KEPCO 3Y is 41.7bp over (89th, average 34bp) and BBB- minus AA- 582bp (70th). Credit is steady and the KOSPI dip was small.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI holds its rebound to Nov 17; no trigger hit.

watch: Next: the US 30Y auction (Nov 12, New York), US PPI (Nov 13), the KTB 50Y auction (Nov 13) and KRW 2.2tn 10Y auction (Nov 16) after the dealer fines, the college entrance exam on Nov 19 (KRX opens an hour late), Nov 1–20 exports around Nov 23, the BOK decision on Nov 26 (hike to 3.25% priced) and the FOMC on Dec 8–9; a hot PPI would hit KTBs at about 0.4–0.55bp per Treasury bp.
